title: seva as vocation
hook: a week of goodbyes ends with a student carrying the work away, and the track names what he carries: seva

segments.voice: Yesterday closed the Uddhava Gita and its week of karma: do all your work for him, slowly, and Uddhava walks off toward Badari. Which task did you slow down? Day one thousand two hundred eight.
screen: `ALL YOUR WORK, SLOWLY.` · `THE WEEK, LOOKING BACK.`

segments.voice: A whole week of one long goodbye. This week Uddhava asked to go with Krishna and was given a teaching instead. The earth taught a wanderer not to swerve when pushed. Krishna gave the path of action to people who still want things. An old beggar, mocked in the street, refused to blame even karma. Workers were sorted by what drives them, not by their jobs. And at the end came the gentle answer: do all your work for me, slowly. Then Uddhava left, carrying it. What do you call a whole life built out of that last line? The track's next word has an answer: seva.
screen: `A WEEK OF ONE LONG GOODBYE.` → `ALL YOUR WORK, FOR HIM.` → `WHAT DO YOU CALL THAT LIFE?`

segments.voice: Seva means service: attending on someone, honoring them by caring for them. In Hindu temples, it's the word for the care given to the deity and to the people who come, from cooking to sweeping to stringing flowers. And the word reaches back into the texts. In the Bhagavata's seventh book, the boy Prahlada lists the ways a person can love Vishnu: hearing about him, singing of him, remembering him, and then serving his feet, worship, bowing, being his servant, being his friend, and offering oneself completely. Serving and servanthood sit right in the middle of that list. Seva, in other words, isn't a side project of devotion. It's one of its main rooms. Now the second half of today's title: vocation. Near the end of the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna says that a person who worships the source of all beings through their own work, the work that is theirs to do, reaches perfection. Read that next to the Uddhava Gita's last lesson and the two fit together. Uddhava was told to do all his work for Krishna. The Gita says the work itself, done as worship, is the offering. That's seva as vocation: not a few hours of good deeds squeezed in around a job, but the job, the household, the caring, all of it done as service. The next few days look at that idea from several sides: in a tree, in a hungry king, and in an honored guest who washed feet at a great feast.
screen: `SEVA: SERVICE, ATTENDING ON.` · `PRAHLADA: SERVING, SERVANTHOOD.` · `WORSHIP HIM WITH YOUR OWN WORK.` · `NOT BESIDE THE JOB: THE JOB ITSELF.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: find the seva already in your week. Settle, and breathe. Go back over the last few days slowly. Where did your work, paid or unpaid, actually serve someone? A meal made, a report someone needed, a ride given. Don't inflate it. Just find one. Hold that person in mind for a while, and let the work become, for a moment, something you gave. If you pray, you can offer that work to the One you pray to. The bell holds the time.
Seva as vocation. Seva is service, attending on God and on others. As a vocation, it's a life's work done as that kind of service. Today's word.
Your line: seva as vocation. Today, before you start your work, name one person it will serve. Day one thousand two hundred eight.

howItsDone: In Hindu temples and homes, seva names the care given to the deity and to others, such as cooking, cleaning and preparing flowers, and some Hindus describe their daily work itself as seva offered to God.

fork.setup: you have a job you need, not one anyone would call holy. what does the Gita's verse about your own work suggest?
options: quit and look for a holier job.
worship through the work you already have.
keep work and worship strictly apart.
fork.reveal: the Gita says a person reaches perfection by worshiping the source of all beings through their own work. the job itself can be seva.

original.note: Sanskrit: service, attendance; honoring someone by caring for them.

trapdoor: what you thought: seva is a volunteer shift on the weekend.
what it means: service offered as worship, and, as a vocation, a whole life's work offered that way.
what a scholar hears: pada-sevana and dasya in Prahlada's list (Bhagavata Purana 7.5.23), read with Bhagavad Gita 18.46, worshiping him through one's own work.
